candidate.title: Potential unused viewport capacity
candidate.reason: Measured text, control and media bounds occupy less than the discovery threshold while rendered text continues below the fold.
candidate.suggestion: Review whether useful task information could be visible together. Explain intentional whitespace or propose a scoped requirement for review; do not fill space, shrink type or change rules merely to remove this flag.

metrics.limitations: Geometry is advisory, not information relevance or design approval. Media/control bounds count allocated space, not painted content. CSS background images, pseudo-elements, shadow text and occlusion are not assessed.

taskImpact.established: The task preserves current readings, next action, four schedule events and six historical observations on a read-only status page.
taskImpact.assumption: Recent history helps interpret the current reading; treating the complete six-observation window as initial desktop context is a proposed requirement, not an existing obligation.
taskImpact.observed: The last history row crosses the 900 CSS-pixel initial viewport boundary while the overview and schedule distribute small amounts of text across a wide area.

interpretation.rationale: A compact counterpart exposes the entire finite observation set at the same viewport while retaining all facts and passing the existing keyboard/refresh/preservation checks. This supports reviewing the information grouping; it does not establish overall design approval.

proposedRequirement.expected: Show current readings, next action, all four schedule events and all six recent observations in the initial desktop view. Diagnostic details may remain disclosed.

check.note: Retain the existing exact-fact, readable-type and behavior checks. Author this boundary only after acceptance; it is not applied in this trial.

limits: One local host-agent interpretation; no blinded or general model-efficacy claim.
Removing the geometric flag alone does not prove useful density.
